CITY OF

  Council Member  Council Member

All agenda items and reports are available for review in the City Clerk’s Office and www.hpca.gov. Any writings
or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda (other than writings
legally exempt from public disclosure) will be made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk
located at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to
5:30 p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including auxiliary aids or services,
in order to participate in the public meeting may request such modification, accommodation, aid or service by
contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by
telephone at (323) 584-6230. Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT WHILE COUNCIL IS IN
SESSION. Thank you.
 PLEASE NOTE--The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City
Council. Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order
and decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of the
City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park City
  Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each speaker
  will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed on the City
  Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct disruptive
  to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of Procedure or
  conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must be
  directed to the Mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required for
the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

Public Comment

Certain provisions of the Brown Act are temporarily waived pursuant to Governor Newsom’s
Executive Order N-25-20 and N-29-20.

In the interest of Public Health and Safety in order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus,
you are strongly encouraged to observe the City Council meetings on the City of Huntington Park’s
website at www.hpca.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENT – If you would like to comment on any listed Agenda Items or Non-Agenda
Items, please email the City Clerk’s office at publiccomment@hpca.gov or by telephone, by calling
(323) 584-6230, up until one (1) hour, prior to the start of the meeting. Public Comments will
then be read during public comment and made part of the record.

The City of Huntington Park thanks you in advance for your cooperation.

For both open and closed session, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per Huntington
Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other speakers and
may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one meeting to another.
This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled public hearing items.

All comments or queries shall be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown Act,
no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing on the
posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide direction to staff,
or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA

 Additions/Deletions to Agenda

Items of business may be added to the agenda upon a motion adopted by a minimum two-thirds
vote finding that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action came to the
attention of the City or Agency subsequent to the agenda being posted. Items may be deleted
from the agenda upon the request of staff or Council.

Important Notice

The City of Huntington Park shows replays of City Council Meetings on Local Access Channel 3
and over the Internet at www.hpca.gov. NOTE: Your attendance at this public meeting may result
in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice.

  MINUTES

  Regular Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Tuesday, October 20, 2020

The City Council conducted this meeting in accordance with California Governor
Newsom's Executive Order N-25-20 and N-29-20.

The Rules of Decorum were played prior to the start of the Regular Meeting.

The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
called to order at 6:02 p.m. on Tuesday, October 20, 2020, in the Council Chambers at
City Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Manuel "Manny" Avila
presiding.

PRESENT: Council Member(s): Eduardo "Eddie" Martinez, Marilyn Sanabria, Karina
Macias, Vice Mayor Graciela Ortiz, and Mayor Manuel "Manny" Avila.

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: Ricardo Reyes, City Manager; Raul Alvarez, Assistant City
Manager; Araceli Almazan, City Attorney; Sergio lnfanzon, Director of Community
Development/Acting City Clerk; Cesar Roldan, Director of Public Works; Cynthia
Norzagaray, Director of Parks and Recs; Cosme Lozano, Chief of Police; ABSENT: Nita
McKay, Director of Finance & Administrative Services

INVOCATION

Invocation was led by Council Member Martinez.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Macias.

PRESENTATIONS  No Presentations

PUBLIC COMMENT

  1. Chris Chai submitted a request to vote No on the State Measure 16 and asked
  to help stop discrimination of any race in our community and in our state.

  2. Terry Fung submitted an email vote No on Measure 16. He urged the City
  Council to take a position to oppose the measure.

  3. Miguel Vargas a lifelong resident of Huntington Park invited all residents to
  participate of a care webinar organized by TreePeople on Thursday, October
  22 at 5:30 p.m. via zoom. Mr. Vargas asked the City Council to share the flyers
  and information about the vent.

  4. Mr. John Longoria submitted a request to remind the City Council about revising
  the in-lieu parking fee ordinance

  1. No staff response

City Manager Ricardo Reyes introduced the item and Mayor Avila announced the public
hearing.

City Attorney announced that it was appropriate for the mayor to open for public hearing
to discuss item Ten. Attorney Almazan also stated that under normal circumstances the
Mayor presents the question to everyone present, whether they have any comments
regarding item ten, but given that we are in the middle of the pandemic and that city
council meeting are currently close to members of the public. The mayor needed to ask
the city clerk if any comments from the public were received. Mayor Avila opened the
public hearing and asked if there were any questions associated to item ten. City Clerk
responded that no additional comments were submitted by the public and that all
comments had been incorporated into the consolidated plan.

City Manager, Ricardo Reyes, added that comments were received and adjustments
were made, and the only adjustment that needed to be made was to allocate $50,000 for
food pantry to cover three (3) food giveaways in the Parks and Recreation Department

$523,614.00, that's the only change that was made from the previous reading.

2020/21 annual action plan, and citizen participation plan, seconded by Council

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS -

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Council Member Martinez thanked the staff for making sure the council meeting was
conducted safely. To all the families be strong stay well and make the best decisions to
wear a mask during these difficulty times. He also thanked those who completed the
Census and stated that a report will be presented on November. He congratulated the LA
Lakers for becoming champions!

Council Member Sanabria thanked all the staff for all the hard work, and wished the
Dodgers good luck. She asked everyone to be safe, celebrate safely, especially during
this pandemic, and celebrate at home.

Council Member Macias thanked staff for their hard work. She also reminded everyone
about a food distribution activity on Saturday October 24, 2020 from 8:30 a.m. - 11:00
a.m. CM Macias thanked Tzu Chi USA foundation that has been collaborating with Gage
Middle School having monthly food distributions. In addition, she reminded everyone to
vote early.

Vice Mayor Ortiz thanked everyone for their hard work. She gave a special thank you to
the Acting City Clerk for advocating for our community to be able to get enough voting
centers. She stated that unfortunately, LA County didn't provide enough voting centers,
and the City was going to have only two centers. Vice Mayor Ortiz wanted the residents
to know that they were going to continue fighting for equity, making sure we could get a
third voting center. She also sent a message to those watching the meeting at home and
she stated that it is our right to vote. Please vote early, lines will be long, please take
advantage of the 5 days in case we are not able to get the third voting center. "Given that
there are cities that have almost the same amount of register voters than our City and
they have seven vote centers versus our two centers, it just tells us how we still have an
issue of systemic racism. We will continue to fight for our community and will continue to
advocate for you. Big thank you to Sergio lnfanzon for trying to advocate as much as he
could on the City's behalf for our residents. At this point, it has to be us community leaders
to step in and advocate for our community." Thank you staff for continue to advocate for
our residents day in day out.

ADJOURNMENT

Mayor Avila thanked Chief Lozano for taking care of the city with the Lakers and Dodgers
and all the excitement behind their championships. People are tired of being at home,
they want to go out and express their excitement. Thank you! Mayor Avila reminded
everyone about the three big issues that we still have: the virus, census and the voting.
There all three important things we need to take care before the end of the year.

are helping and fighting against the corona virus.

Respectfully submitted,

Sergio lnfanzon
